---
title: "Is the aircraft pitch stable?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
ENTRY_CEILING = 20.0
SOLVE_BUDGET = 15.0
PROBE_POOL = 120.0
PROBE_SPENT = 39.0

import aerosandbox as asb
import aerosandbox.numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.interpolate import interp1d

airplane = get_airplane()
op0 = asb.OperatingPoint(velocity=10, alpha=0)

# Find neutral point at alpha=0
aero_np = asb.AeroBuildup(airplane, op0).run_with_stability_derivatives(alpha=True)
x_np = aero_np["x_np"][0]
c_ref = airplane.c_ref

# Set CG for 10% static margin
x_cg = x_np - 0.1 * c_ref
airplane.xyz_ref = [x_cg, 0, airplane.xyz_ref[2]]

aero0 = asb.AeroBuildup(airplane, op0).run_with_stability_derivatives(alpha=True)
Cma = aero0["Cma"][0]

alphas = np.linspace(-5, 5, 21)
op = asb.OperatingPoint(velocity=10, alpha=alphas)
aero = asb.AeroBuildup(airplane, op).run()

trim_alpha = float(interp1d(aero["Cm"], alphas)(0))
```

**Answer.** Yes, but it will dive. With the center of gravity placed for a 10% static margin ([`{python} f"{x_cg * 1000:.0f}"`]{.key} mm), the aircraft is statically stable in pitch ($\partial C_m / \partial \alpha =$ [`{python} f"{Cma:.2f}"`]{.key} rad⁻¹). However, because the main fuselage is curved upwards and the wings are symmetric flat plates, the aircraft has a negative pitching moment at zero angle of attack. It therefore trims at [`{python} f"{trim_alpha:.1f}"`]{.key}° with negative lift, meaning it dives rather than gliding (@fig-cm-alpha).

::: {.callout-tip}

```{python}
#| label: fig-cm-alpha
#| fig-cap: "Pitching moment coefficient against angle of attack. The negative intercept means the stable trim point is at a negative angle."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
ax.plot(alphas, aero["Cm"], ".-")
ax.axhline(0, color="k", linewidth=0.5)
ax.axvline(trim_alpha, color="r", linestyle="--", label=f"Trim $\\alpha$ = {trim_alpha:.1f}°")
ax.set_xlabel(r"Angle of attack $\alpha$ [deg]")
ax.set_ylabel(r"Pitching moment $C_m$")
ax.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
